title: Service of Process
logline: Don Fax faxes Rivet a final notice on a notary who served the Family by email, and Krump steals the credit over the radio.
goal: Kill Stamp on the courthouse steps and collect Don Fax's nine hundred from the booth.
whyNotFiller: The paper-jam FUCK is the laugh, Stamp asking to be signed in halves is paperwork used as a weapon, and Krump claiming the corpse on the radio is the turn that opens his housekeeping questline while Don Fax never names who else is copied.

characters.name: Stamp
characters.designNote: Waist-high notary robot with a rubber-stamp head, a red ink-pad chest, and a paper scroll for a tail; the stamp face reads clearly from above.

beats.title: The booth
beats.summary: A payphone rings. Patch routes it and hangs up, and Don Fax's final notice prints out of the coin slot and jams.

beats.title: The steps
beats.summary: Rivet climbs the courthouse steps, and Stamp tries to notarize the welder into two neat halves.

beats.title: The credit
beats.summary: Krump comes on the radio, takes the credit, and offers the next housekeeping cheque. CRUMB FM burns him for it. Don Fax pays at the booth.

lines.speaker: patch
lines.text: You there? Job. Courthouse steps. Party says paper. Click.

lines.speaker: don-fax
lines.text: PER MY LAST FAX: the recipient served this Family by email, kid, and email is a disease. Point one, his stamp. Point two, his face. Point three, see points one and two. Hold on, paper jam. FUCK. My soul has a paper jam. That was an act of God. Regards.

lines.speaker: rivet
lines.text: Courthouse. I clock in.

lines.speaker: rivet
lines.text: Steps are dirty. I go up.

lines.speaker: stamp
lines.text: Hold still, signer. This is service. Sign here, sign there, sign in halves.

lines.speaker: rivet
lines.text: Signed in halves. Clocking out.

lines.speaker: general-krump
lines.text: Son, that appliance you decommissioned was a dangerous rogue with OPINIONS, and my budget has already written your next housekeeping cheque, which I will be presenting to myself. Krump out.

lines.speaker: rivet
lines.text: Not your unit.

lines.speaker: mc-crumbtray
lines.text: CRUMB FM nation, the Mystery Welder just notarized a man into pieces! POP! Holy (bleep) shit, listeners, the General Malfunction is taking credit for a stamp!

lines.speaker: don-fax
lines.text: Point one, the recipient is filed. Point two, nine hundred dollars, laminated thanks enclosed. Point three, see point one. Regards.

lines.speaker: rivet
lines.text: Nine hundred. Shift's done.

mechanics.name: Payphone job router
mechanics.summary: A booth rings, Patch routes the party, and Don Fax's notice prints from the coin slot.

mechanics.name: Heat
mechanics.summary: Killing Stamp on the steps raises heat to 2. A second wave arrives if Rivet lingers.

mechanics.name: Diegetic radio
mechanics.summary: Krump cuts in to claim the kill, and CRUMB FM mocks him on the same band.

failStates: Stamp reaches the mail truck and serves the block

title: Never a Scratch
logline: The Valet has Rivet retrieve a general's staff car from impound, and the dead driver in the seat wakes as Gearbox.
goal: Relocate the staff car from the municipal impound to bay nine and leave with Gearbox awake.
whyNotFiller: Gearbox's calm Mirror-signal-MURDER while he grabs the wheel is the laugh in the hands, Krump insisting he invented beige is the vanity joke, and the dead driver staying in Rivet's head unlocks soul 1.

beats.title: The ticket
beats.summary: The Valet hands over a ticket for a general's staff car as if Rivet were collecting a dinner guest.

beats.title: The impound
beats.summary: Rivet turns the key in the impound lockup. The driver who was on break wakes up and takes an interest in the wheel.

beats.title: The ramp
beats.summary: Krump's jeeps chase the car. At the Choir band Gearbox grabs the wheel, and Rivet wrestles the stick or lets him have the ramp.

beats.title: Bay nine
beats.summary: The curb leaves a mark. The Valet swears, then denies it, and Gearbox does not get out.

lines.speaker: the-valet
lines.text: Would sir be so kind as to retrieve her from level three, sir?

lines.speaker: the-valet
lines.text: The previous driver was a general's aide, sir.

lines.speaker: rivet
lines.text: Municipal impound. I drive.

lines.speaker: gearbox
lines.text: Buddy, turn it, turn it, I have the wheel — wait, whose beige is this, pal, whose beige is on the seats?

lines.speaker: rivet
lines.text: The car talks. I did not order that.

lines.speaker: general-krump
lines.text: Son, that staff car is LIBERTY on wheels, and the appliance driving her knew things about beige, a color I personally invented for the motor pool. Krump out.

lines.speaker: gearbox
lines.text: Brake, BRAKE, the other brake, buddy, the jeep is in the mirror and in the cupholder — oh fuck oh fuck, did you check your six?

lines.speaker: gearbox
lines.text: Mirror, signal, MURDER.

lines.speaker: rivet
lines.text: Clocking out.

lines.speaker: the-valet
lines.text: The curb has left a — fucking — mark on her door, sir.

lines.speaker: the-valet
lines.text: Never a scratch, sir. Enjoy your evening.

lines.speaker: gearbox
lines.text: I'm on break, buddy, a long break, and the route is ours now — wait, is it ours, pal, did you check the mirror?

lines.speaker: rivet
lines.text: Gearbox stays. I drive.

mechanics.name: Driving
mechanics.summary: Rivet drives the staff car from the impound lockup to bay nine while jeeps pursue.

mechanics.name: Gearbox car manipulation
mechanics.summary: Turning the key wakes Gearbox. He backseat-drives, and at Choir he grabs the wheel for one beat.

mechanics.name: Choir grab-the-wheel
mechanics.summary: At the Choir band Gearbox takes the ramp. Rivet wrestles the stick or gives him the wheel.

failStates: The impound cordon closes on the car
